model.rationale: The district's 25-point Democratic lean, Haynes's roughly 27-to-1 fundraising advantage, and market pricing near 96% all point the same direction, and nothing in the evidence suggests a competitive race.
model.watch: Any poll showing a single-digit race or a surge of Republican outside spending for Jackson would be the main signal of movement, though nothing currently points that way.

overview:
TX-30 is an open seat in a Dallas-area district drawn with a Democratic lean of about 25 points. With no incumbent on the ballot, Democrat Frederick Haynes III faces Republican Everett Jackson in the general election. Haynes has raised roughly $695,000 and holds about $159,000 on hand, supplemented by about $200,000 in outside support, while Jackson has raised about $25,000 with minimal cash remaining.

No public polls cover the race and no expert raters have ranked it, so the outlook rests on the district's fundamentals, the fundraising gap, and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win near 96%. The combination of the seat's strong partisan lean and the candidates' stark resource disparity points to the district remaining in Democratic hands by a wide margin in November.
